name: Jinwutuan (劲舞团, Audition)
blurb: The Korean dance rhythm game that filled Chinese internet cafés from 2005
title: What Is Jinwutuan (劲舞团)? Audition Online in 2000s China
description: Jinwutuan (劲舞团) is the Chinese Audition Online, a Korean dance rhythm game run in China by 9you since 2005, with over 780,000 players online at its peak.
answer: Jinwutuan (劲舞团) is the Chinese edition of Audition Online, a dance rhythm game developed by South Korea's T3 Entertainment and run in China by Shanghai-based 9you (久游网), which opened it to the public on 12 May 2005. Players type arrow-key sequences and hit the space bar on the beat to make their avatars dance, and the game doubled as a social space with couples and in-game weddings. Around 2007 it had more than 780,000 players online at once; it cooled afterwards, but the PC game was still running in China in 2026.

body: After choosing a song, a row of arrows appears at the bottom of the screen. You type the matching arrow keys, then press the space bar (or Ctrl) as a moving marker hits the beat. Accurate timing earns a "Perfect" and a flashy dance move; mistakes earn a "Miss". Later bars bring longer, faster sequences, and expert players' finger speed was a spectacle in internet cafés.

There were solo, team and couple modes, and a marriage system. Hair, clothes and accessories could all be changed, many of them paid items, and players chatted in the room between songs, so for many teenagers it was also an early online social network. Reports say its controls were inspired by the PlayStation game Bust a Groove.

What happened
rows: Chinese open beta on 12 May: reportedly 1 million sign-ups and 80,000 concurrent players on day one; later listed by the Ministry of Culture among games suitable for minors
Over 780,000 concurrent players; registered accounts reportedly peaked at 540 million
Licensed mobile version launched, later renamed Jinwu Shidai and published by NetEase
9you renews its long-term license for the PC game with T3
The mobile game is scheduled to close on 1 June; the PC game keeps running

body: The peak came around 2007. Competing dance games multiplied, internet cafés and PC games gave way to mobile games, and the original players grew up. 9you's revenue fell for years and the company shrank sharply.

The game was closely tied to the feizhuliu "non-mainstream" youth style and had a poor reputation with parents and media at the time, and in 2008 the Ministry of Culture publicly criticized it. Today it is remembered mostly as a piece of 2000s internet-café culture.

faq.a: Yes. According to 2026 reports the PC game is still operated in China by 9you. The mobile spin-off was scheduled to shut down on 1 June 2026.

faq.q: Is Jinwutuan the same game as Audition?
faq.a: Yes. Jinwutuan is the Chinese name for Audition Online, developed by T3 Entertainment in South Korea and released in many countries under different publishers.
Arrow keys to enter the dance sequence shown on screen, then the space bar (or Ctrl) on the beat to perform it.
